tagline: 37 million people wrapped around a bay, an airport on the water, chronic congestion — and almost no commuter water-transit. The biggest under-used metro waterfront on earth.
summary: Greater Tokyo is the largest metro area on earth (~37M) wrapped around Tokyo Bay, yet the bay and the Sumida River carry an almost trivial share of trips. The Tokyo Water Bus runs sightseeing routes (Asakusa–Hinode–Odaiba) and there are limited commuter experiments, but for a waterfront megacity the water is dramatically under-used. Meanwhile congestion is chronic, Haneda Airport sits right on the bay, and continued Odaiba/Toyosu/Harumi Flag waterfront build-out is adding bayfront population. The opportunity is three layers: urban commuter + tourism on the Sumida and inner bay, an airport-access bay shortcut (Haneda↔central waterfront/Yokohama), and cross-bay city links to Yokohama. Japan's exacting safety/certification culture rewards a rigorously-engineered, software-defined, zero-emission platform.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire inner-bay + Sumida + cross-bay network — Hinode↔Asakusa, ↔Odaiba/Toyosu/Harumi, ↔Haneda, Tokyo↔Yokohama (~14 nm), ↔Chiba — sits comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with terminal charging.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 2,000 nm hybrid range covers the bay-mouth and leisure corridors — Yokosuka/Boso (~26 nm) and the Izu peninsula/Oshima (~55 nm) — with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

competitive_landscape: The bay is served today by the Tokyo Water Bus / Tokyo Cruise sightseeing fleet and limited commuter experiments, plus dense commercial port traffic. Demand for real commuter water-transit is almost entirely latent. There is no foiling incumbent — and Japan's rigorous safety/certification culture rewards a software-defined, zero-emission, precisely-engineered platform.
seasonality: Operable most of the year; binding variables are typhoon season (Aug–Oct), winter north winds and summer bay chop. Foiling above the chop is an advantage; typhoon windows are the dominant blackout class.
regulatory_note: Japan Coast Guard / JCI (Japan Craft Inspection) + JG class govern vessel certification; the Port of Tokyo and Port of Yokohama authorities manage the harbours; the Tokyo Metropolitan Government sets waterfront/transit policy. Exacting safety/certification expectations are the primary gate — a market that rewards the rigorously-engineered platform story.
signature_routes: Tokyo ↔ Yokohama / Minato Mirai (cross-bay city link)
Tokyo Bay ↔ Izu peninsula / Oshima (hybrid leisure line-haul, ~55 nm)

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of inter-island mobility at national scale — the proof that a foiling fleet can be the transport layer, not a novelty.
